issue.title: History search lowercases a copy of every field it checks
issue.body:
## Summary

`HistoryEntry::matches` (`src/history.rs`) lowercases a fresh copy of each field it checks:

```rust
let matches_field = |field: &str| field.to_lowercase().contains(needle);
```

A query that matches nothing allocates about 40k strings per search over 10,000 entries: raw text, final text, application, model, and profile. `raw_text` is usually identical to `final_text`, so it's searched twice.

## Measured

Old matching over the `perf/seeds/history.ts` shape (10,000 entries), `hex` at opt-level 3, macOS arm64, 1,000 runs per query:

| query | per search |
|---|---|
| `c` | 22 µs |
| `cache` | 84–108 µs |
| `cache key` (0 results) | **4.1–5.2 ms** |

`history-search` runs one per key typed (one key every 120 ms).

## Expected

Same results without an allocation per field.

issue.title: History searches again on every frame, even when nothing changed
issue.body:
## Summary

`HistoryPane::poll` (`src/rune_ui/history.rs`) runs before every frame and on every 250 ms tick while History shows. Each call runs `store.search(..)` again, clones up to 200 entries, and compares them with the previous list, even when neither the query nor the store changed.

```rust
let previous = std::mem::take(&mut self.entries);
self.reload_entries();               // store.search(&self.searched), every poll
let changed = self.entries != previous;
```

With a query that matches nothing, each poll scans all 10,000 entries.

## Measured

`History::search` over the `perf/seeds/history.ts` shape (10,000 entries), with `hex` built at opt-level 3, macOS arm64:

| query | per poll |
|---|---|
| `""` | 65 µs |
| `cache` | 144 µs |
| `cache key` (0 results, full scan) | **3.3 ms** |

At that cost, every frame of `history-scroll` and every tick of `history-search` pays a full scan.

## Expected

Search again only when the query changed or the store did (record, delete, change, prune, retention, another process's write).

issue.title: macOS: the main-thread pump wakes every 16 ms while idle
issue.body:
## Summary

On macOS the main-thread pump (`src/macos_rune.rs`) runs on a repeating 16 ms `NSTimer` for the life of the app. Most ticks just call `try_recv` on empty channels. The HUD needs a frame-rate tick only while it animates (`follow_pointer`); the rest of the time this is ~62 wakeups/s on the main thread for nothing.

```rust
const PUMP_INTERVAL: f64 = 0.016;
NSTimer::scheduledTimerWithTimeInterval_repeats_block(PUMP_INTERVAL, true, &block)
```

## Impact

Tray idle (`perf/idle.bench.ts#window-closed`, `cpu.wakes`), window idle, and `listening-at-rest` all pay for it. By my count it's about 75% of the tray's timer wakeups.

## Expected

Tick every frame only while the HUD animates. Otherwise, idle at a slow pace and let whatever sends the pump something (HUD events, menu actions, `hex` control calls, input-source changes) wake it at once.

issue.title: perf: <BS> runs regex compares for rules that can never delete
issue.body:
## Summary

`<BS>` becomes slow on long lines when regex `only_cr` rules are loaded (e.g. the endwise rules). `autopairs_delete` copies the line and runs an unanchored `string.match` for every such rule, but these rules have `del_cond = false`, so `can_del` always returns `false` and the work is thrown away.

## Where

`lua/nvim-autopairs.lua`, `autopairs_delete`: `text_cusor_line` + `utils.compare` run before `rule:can_del(...)`. For `is_regex` rules, `text_cusor_line` returns the whole line prefix/suffix, so each compare is O(line length).

## Measurements

Headless nvim, `filetype=lua`, default rules + `endwise-lua` (9 buffer rules, 3 regex endwise), cursor at end of line, avg of 2000 calls to `autopairs_bs()`:

| line length | `<BS>` with endwise rules | `<BS>` without endwise rules |
|---|---|---|
| 100 | 3.0 µs | — |
| 5,000 | 64 µs | — |
| 100,000 | 1,546 µs | 7 µs |

Cost scales linearly with line length × number of regex `only_cr` rules, so users with many endwise rules on long lines (minified JS/JSON, generated code) pay it on every backspace.

## Proposed fix

Skip rules whose `del_cond` can never pass (anything other than a table or function, mirroring `can_do`) before computing prev/next text.

issue.title: perf: Filters:custom calls getcwd for every file, even with no custom filters
issue.body:
**Problem**

`Filters:custom` calls `vim.uv.cwd()` for every file that gets scanned, via `utils.path_relative(path, vim.uv.cwd())` (`lua/nvim-tree/explorer/filters.lua:180`). This happens even when `filters.custom` is empty, the default, so the result is never used.

`getcwd` is slow on some platforms: about **61µs per call on macOS**.

**Impact** (profile on master)

| Operation | Share of time on this line |
|---|---|
| `api.tree.expand_all()` | 33% |
| `Explorer:reload_explorer()` | 42% |

**Proposed fix**

- Return early from `Filters:custom` when there are no custom patterns.
- Resolve the cwd once per directory in `Filters:prepare`, and only when there are custom patterns.

Filtering behaviour stays the same.

Happy to follow up with a PR as soon as I get some time.


**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: reload_explorer runs git status synchronously, blocking the UI
issue.body:
**Problem**

`Explorer:reload_explorer()` and `Explorer:reload_git()` call `git.reload_all_projects()`. That runs `git status` synchronously for every known repository and blocks the UI through `vim.wait` in `GitRunner:wait`.

These reloads are triggered by:
- `BufEnter` with `reload_on_bufenter`, or when the cwd changed,
- `BufWritePost` with `auto_reload_on_write` and no filesystem watchers,
- `FugitiveChanged` and `NeogitStatusRefreshed`,
- `BufReadPost` and `BufUnload` with `filters.no_buffer`,
- filter toggles and marks changes,
- file operations: paste, rename, remove, trash,
- `api.tree.reload()`, `api.git.reload()`.

**Impact**

On the test repo, a synchronous `git status` takes around 25-55ms per repository. On large monorepos it can take hundreds of milliseconds, up to `git.timeout`, freezing nvim for that time.

The watcher path (`git.refresh_dir`) already uses the async `GitRunner` callback.

**Proposed change**

Run the reload's git status asynchronously, as `refresh_dir` does, and refresh and redraw in the callback. Keep the existing `event_running` guard, or replace it with a debounce, so that overlapping reloads don't stack.

Happy to follow up with a PR as soon as I get some time.

**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: watcher is_git resolves paths with fnamemodify when GIT_DIR is unset
issue.body:
**Problem**

`is_git` in `lua/nvim-tree/explorer/watch.lua` runs for every `DirectoryNode` that gets a watcher. When `GIT_DIR` is unset, it still calls `vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":p")` and `vim.fn.fnamemodify(nil, ":p")`. It then calls `vim.fn.fnamemodify(path, ":t")`.

**Impact**

About **68µs per directory** on macOS. Once the custom filter and git toplevel costs are removed, this is about 9% of `expand_all`.

**Proposed fix**

- Only resolve paths when `GIT_DIR` is set.
- Use `utils.path_basename` instead of `fnamemodify(path, ":t")`.

Same result.

Happy to follow up with a PR as soon as I get some time.

**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: filetype sorter calls vim.filetype.match on every comparison
issue.body:
**Problem**

With `sort.sorter = "filetype"`, `Sorter:filetype` calls `vim.filetype.match` twice per comparison. A merge sort makes O(n log n) comparisons, and `vim.filetype.match` is expensive.

The `sort.sorter` function path also calls `vim.filetype.match` once per node.

**Impact**

Sorting a directory with 3.3k entries took **4459ms** on master. This runs on every reload of that directory.

**Proposed fix**

Resolve each name's filetype once per sort, using a cache that is rebuilt on every sort so that `vim.filetype.add` changes still apply. In testing this brings the same sort down to 532ms, with identical ordering.

**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: renderer highlights via vim.hl.range are slow on large trees
issue.body:
**Problem**

`Renderer:render_hl` applies every highlight of every line with `vim.hl.range`. That function is generic: on each call it switches buffer context with `vim._with`, calls `col('$')` twice and calls `getregionpos`. nvim-tree's ranges are always single-line byte ranges, so none of that work is needed.

**Impact**

| | µs per highlight |
|---|---|
| `vim.hl.range` | 6.1 |
| `nvim_buf_set_extmark` | 0.74 |

At 16.8k visible lines, `render_hl` is about **50%** of `Renderer:draw()` (620ms) and about 15% of `reload_explorer`.

**Proposed fix**

Call `nvim_buf_set_extmark` directly with the same ranges and the same priority (`vim.hl.priorities.user`). The highlights produced are identical. Happy to provide a PR for this ofc.

**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: is_executable calls fs_access for every file on every reload
issue.body:
**Problem**

`utils.is_executable` calls `vim.uv.fs_access(path, "X")` for:
- every new `FileNode`, and
- every existing node on every `Explorer:reload`.

The node's `lstat` result is already available at both call sites.

**Impact**

`fs_access` costs 7.7µs per call vs 1.9µs for `lstat`. `is_executable` is about **11%** of `reload_explorer` on a fully expanded 16.8k-node tree.

**Proposed fix**

Pass the existing stat into `is_executable`. A regular file with none of the user, group or other execute bits set can never pass `access(X)`, even as root, so return false without the syscall. Files with execute bits, directories and links still use `fs_access`, happy to follow up with a PR soon.



**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: perf: git rev-parse is spawned for every directory loaded
issue.body:
**Problem**

`git.get_toplevel` caches its result per path. Every directory loaded for the first time is therefore a cache miss, and each miss spawns `git rev-parse --show-toplevel --absolute-git-dir` synchronously.

Expanding a tree with about 900 directories spawns about 900 git processes, one at a time.

**Impact** (profile on master)

`api.tree.expand_all()` took **20.5s**. Spawning and waiting for `git rev-parse` accounted for about **33%** of it.

**Proposed fix**

Directories are loaded top down, so the parent's toplevel is almost always cached already. A directory with no `.git` entry of its own (a directory, or a file for submodules and worktrees) is in the same repository as its parent, or in none if the parent is in none. In that case, reuse the parent's cached result.

Fall back to `git rev-parse` when:
- the directory has its own `.git`,
- the parent is not cached, or
- `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_WORK_TREE` is set.

Nested repositories keep their own toplevel.

Happy to fix this with a PR, at least by eow.

**Environment:** macOS, Nvim v0.13.0-dev, LuaJIT 2.1. Test repo: 16.8k files and folders, 3.1k `git status` entries (modified, untracked, ignored). Measured headless with `vim.uv.hrtime()` and the LuaJIT profiler (`jit.p`).

issue.title: refresh() is ~20x slower for non-current buffers due to unused fold lookups
issue.body:
### Problem

`refresh()` is ~20x slower for a buffer that is not the current buffer.

For every line in the viewport, `refresh()` calls `utils.get_foldclosed(bufnr, row)`. For a non-current buffer this does `get_win()` + `nvim_win_call()`, which costs ~130 us per call. But the result is only used behind `is_current_buffer and ...` checks, so for non-current buffers it is computed and thrown away.

https://github.com/lukas-reineke/indent-blankline.nvim/blob/f1e186e/lua/ibl/init.lua#L346-L359

With ~130 lines rendered (viewport + `viewport_buffer`), that is ~17 ms of wasted work per refresh. Non-current refreshes happen on `scrollbind`, LSP inlay hint responses for background buffers, `TextChanged` in other windows, etc.

Measured with a 4.8k line Lua file, 68 line window, 8 windows open:

| | `refresh()` |
|---|---|
| current buffer | 1.2 ms |
| non-current buffer | **21.5 ms** |

### Steps to reproduce

```lua
-- nvim --clean -u repro.lua big.lua
vim.opt.rtp:prepend "/path/to/indent-blankline.nvim"
vim.bo.filetype = "lua"
require("ibl").setup {}
local buf = vim.api.nvim_get_current_buf()
vim.cmd "vsplit | enew"
local t = vim.uv.hrtime()
for _ = 1, 100 do require("ibl").refresh(buf) end
print((vim.uv.hrtime() - t) / 100 / 1e6 .. " ms")
```

### Expected behavior

Skip the fold lookup when the buffer is not current, since the result is never used. Non-current refresh drops to ~1-2 ms, rendered output is unchanged.

### Neovim version (nvim -v)

NVIM v0.13.0-dev-2016+gdbecb8a6fc

issue.title: perf: every entry allocates caches it rarely uses
issue.body:
## Summary

`entry.new` creates two `cmp.Cache` objects and a `resolved_callbacks` table for every item. Each `cache.new` also creates its own metatable, so that's 7 tables per entry before the item is even read.

Most entries are never shown or resolved. Only `match_cache` is used for every entry.

- Create `entry.cache` and `resolved_callbacks` only when first needed. `_get_word` should use the uncached `_get_overwrite` while the entry is being built, otherwise every item with a `textEdit` creates the cache straight away.
- Share one metatable across all `cmp.Cache` instances.

https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/entry.lua#L56-L69
https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/utils/cache.lua#L6

## Data

CPU time, best of 15–20. Benchmark in #2236.

| Metric | Now | Lazy |
|---|---|---|
| `entry.new` x20k, label only | 30.2 ms | 26.2 ms (-13%) |
| `entry.new` x20k, with `textEdit` | 34.0 ms | 28.6 ms (-16%) |
| Building entries, 6k items, `isIncomplete` | 153.7 ms | 131.9 ms (-14%) |

issue.title: perf: matcher char helpers cost several calls per byte
issue.body:
## Summary

The matcher's inner loops call `char.match` and `char.is_semantic_index` for each byte. Both go through several small helpers (`is_alpha` → `alpha[b] or ALPHA[b]`, `is_symbol` → `is_alnum` → ...), costing up to ~8 function calls per byte.

A 256-entry lowercase table makes `char.match` a single comparison (`LOWER[a] == LOWER[b]`), and `is_semantic_index` can read the byte-class tables directly. Results don't change.

https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/utils/char.lua#L70-L117

## Data

CPU time, best of 20. Benchmark in #2236.

| Metric | Now | Lookup tables |
|---|---|---|
| `matcher.match` x60k | 44.9 ms | 27.2 ms (**-39%**) |
| `get_entries`, 6k items, `isIncomplete` | 69.9 ms | 62.2 ms (-11%) |
| `get_entries`, 20k items, `isIncomplete` | 237.7 ms | 208.5 ms (-12%) |

Checked against the current code: identical results for every byte pair (including `nil`), every 2-byte string, and 210k `matcher.match` calls across the different `matching` options.

issue.title: perf: str.oneline scans strings byte by byte in Lua
issue.body:
## Summary

`str.oneline` looks for `\n` with a Lua loop over every byte. It runs on every entry's `word` when entries are built, and on each menu field. `string.find(text, '\n', 1, true)` does the same search in C.

https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/utils/str.lua#L161-L168

## Data

Time to build entries over 10 keystrokes. CPU time, best of 20. Benchmark in #2236.

| Scenario | Byte loop | `string.find` |
|---|---|---|
| 6k items, `isIncomplete` | 153.7 ms | 143.7 ms (-7%) |
| 20k items, `isIncomplete` | 545.1 ms | 514.9 ms (-6%) |

A small win, but the change is a few lines.

issue.title: perf: ensure_nil walks opaque CompletionItem.data
issue.body:
## Summary

`ensure_nil` also walks `CompletionItem.data`. cmp never reads that field. The LSP spec says it must be preserved between `textDocument/completion` and `completionItem/resolve`, so cmp shouldn't strip `null`s from it either.

Skipping `data` makes resolve send back exactly what the server sent, and avoids walking what is often the deepest table in an item (e.g. rust-analyzer's `imports`).

#2212 was about `labelDetails.description`, which is still handled.

## Data

Time to build entries over 10 keystrokes, compared with in-place `ensure_nil` (#2237). CPU time, best of 20. Benchmark in #2236.

| Scenario | In place | In place, `data` skipped |
|---|---|---|
| 6k items, `isIncomplete` | 113.6 ms | 96.9 ms (-15%) |
| 20k items, `isIncomplete` | 378.6 ms | 325.0 ms (-14%) |

issue.title: perf: ensure_nil deep-copies every completion item
issue.body:
## Summary

`misc.ensure_nil` (added in #2217) deep-copies every completion item and `itemDefaults` on every response, allocating a new table for every nested table. It's now the biggest single cost when building entries, and with `isIncomplete` servers it runs on every keystroke.

Only `vim.NIL` fields need changing. Doing that in place gives the same result without the copies (`entry.fill_defaults` already mutates items in place).

https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/utils/misc.lua#L127-L146
https://github.com/hrsh7th/nvim-cmp/blob/2ffe79f/lua/cmp/source.lua#L363-L368

## Data

Time to build entries over 10 keystrokes. CPU time, best of 20. Benchmark in #2236.

| Scenario | Deep copy | In place |
|---|---|---|
| 6k items, full list | 15.5 ms | 10.3 ms (-33%) |
| 6k items, `isIncomplete` | 153.7 ms | 113.6 ms (-26%) |
| 20k items, `isIncomplete` | 545.1 ms | 378.6 ms (**-31%**) |

`ensure_nil` alone on 20k items: 47.6 ms → 21.5 ms.
